By way of this application under section 482 of the Code of Criminal Procedure, 1973 (hereinafter referred to as "the Cr.P.C."), petitioners have prayed for quashing and setting aside the FIR being CR-No.I-66 of 2014 registered with Vijapur Police Station, Dist. Mehsana for the offences NEUTRAL CITATION R/CR.MA/5689/2014 ORDER DATED: 11/12/2024 undefined punishable under Sections 406, 420, 114, 34 and 120(B) of the Indian Penal Code, 1860 (for short, the IPC).
3.

Brief facts of the case are as under:-

sentences.text: The complainant is running a business in the name of a partnership firm Devnandan Oil Industries and was acquainted with accused No. 1.
This acquaintance led to a friendship between them.
On 29/03/2014, accused No. 1, along with accused Nos. 2, 3, 4, and 5, approached the complainant, expressing their intention to purchase the seven vehicles of cotton.

3.2. Therefore, due to acquaintance with the accused no.1, complainant agreed to supply the goods at the rate of Rs.365/-
per 20 kilos.

On 29/03/2014, vide bill No. 172, cotton weighing 10,195 kilos was loaded onto vehicle No. GJ-8-W-262, amounting to Rs. 1,95,362/-and vide bill No. 173, cotton weighing 10,420 kilos was loaded onto vehicle No. GJ-9-V-7909, amounting to Rs.1,99,674/-.

On 31/03/14, vide bill No.
176, cotton weighing NEUTRAL CITATION R/CR.MA/5689/2014 ORDER DATED: 11/12/2024 undefined 10,255 kilos was loaded onto vehicle No. GJ-9-V-7907, amounting to Rs.1,96,512/-.
3.3. The accused purchased goods totaling of Rs.5,91,548/- and assured the complainant that the payment would be made on 01.04.2014.

When complainant requested payment on the specified date, the accused reassured him that payment would be made within two days, upon further demand, accused No. 2 issued three cheques i.e. a cheque dated 03.04.2014 bearing No.824736 for Rs.1,95,362/- and cheque No.824737 for Rs.1,99,674/- and cheque No.824738 for Rs.6,96,572 /-
drawn on Oriental Bank of Commerce.
3.4. When complainant deposited the said three cheques on 03.04.2014, all were dishonored with an endorsement of "Account blocked found as well as funds insufficient".
Therefore, Complain/FIR came to be registered against present petitioner and other co-accused.

4. Learned advocate for the petitioners submitted that NEUTRAL CITATION R/CR.MA/5689/2014 ORDER DATED: 11/12/2024 undefined present petitioners are wrongly arraigned as accuse persons in the complaint.
It is further submitted that petitioners have no connection with the commission of the crime as alleged in the FIR.
It is also submitted that neither petitioner No.1 nor petitioner No.2 are signatory of the three cheques mentioned in the impugned FIR.
It is further submitted that allegations made in the impugned FIR are purely of civil nature and no case of cheating or criminal breach of trust is made out by complainant in the impugned FIR.

It is further submitted that petitioner No.1 is an Agriculturist and Petitioner No.2 is a Businessman and except the fact that petitioner No.1 had gone to hand over the cheques to the complainant, there are no other allegations made against petitioners.

Learned advocate for the petitioners has relied upon these two decisions,
which are as under:-
a) Kunti and Another v. State of Uttar Pradesh and Another; Criminal Appeal No.1380 of 2023.
b) Vesa Holdings Private Limited v. State of Kerala and others; (2015) 8 SCC 293.

Learned advocate for the petitioners submitted that when NEUTRAL CITATION R/CR.MA/5689/2014 ORDER DATED: 11/12/2024 undefined the dispute is purely of civil nature,
criminal proceedings would not be maintainable.
It is further submitted that if intention to cheat is found or developed later on, the same cannot amount to cheating.
The complainant is required to show that accused persons i.e. petitioners had fraudulent and dishonest intention at the time of making promise or representation.

It is further submitted that breach of contract does not give rise to criminal breach of trust for cheating unless fraudulent or dishonest intention is shown right at the beginning of the transaction.
It is further submitted that petitioners have not taken on rent any Oil Mill along with other co-accused persons.
Petitioners have not entered into any partnership with other co-accused.
It is submitted that accused Nos.3 and 5 contacted complainant through accused No.1 and they have taken delivery of cotton seeds in 7 trucks and sold away in the market.
In the present case, it is submitted that allegations made in the complaint are nothing but a transaction of sell of goods of the material.

In case of breach of contract, for recovery of goods sold and delivered,
remedy is by way of a civil suit and not by way of criminal prosecution.
NEUTRAL CITATION R/CR.MA/5689/2014 ORDER DATED: 11/12/2024 undefined 5.
Per contra, learned APP has submitted that after taking delivery of cotton, cheques which were issued by the accused for the payment got returned.

Complainant went at the mill premises i.e. at the place of Mahadeve Oil Mills and met the owner Mr. Vishnubhai Gangbhai and the said owner informed the complainant that the godown was let out to accused persons and the accused persons after unloading cotton bales, sold out the goods in market.
Learned APP has placed on record Investigation Report dated 11.12.2024 on record and the same is taken on record.

5.1. Learned APP further submitted that the Investigating Officer has recorded the statements of Ashokbhai Gandalal Patel who happens to be friend of petitioner No.1 statement of his brother,
namely, Vishnubhai Gandalal Patel, who is the owner of godown is also recorded.
It is submitted that both the witnesses have supported the allegation of the complainant.

As per the statement of the owner of the godown, accused No.2, namely, applicant No.1 had approached Ashokbhai Gandalal Patel and NEUTRAL CITATION R/CR.MA/5689/2014 ORDER DATED: 11/12/2024 undefined requested to give godown on rent for making an oil mill.
It is further submitted that during the investigation, investigation team has ceased certain part of the material from the godown.

It is therefore submitted that allegation made in the FIR is supported by the statements of the witnesses and when the involvement of the petitioners are prima-facie established, the impugned FIR may not be quashed.
6. I have considered the submissions canvassed by learned advocates for the parties and also considered impugned FIR and also statement of witnesses.
Allegation of the complainant is that all accused persons in connivance with each other have committed an offence of cheating and criminal breach of trust.

It is also alleged that accused Nos.2,3 and 5 with an intention to cheat complainant,
purchased seven cotton bales on 29.3.2014 and 31.3.2014 with a promise to make payment of the goods on 1.4.2014.
Accused issued three different cheques totaling Rs.10,91,608/-.

All the three cheques returned uncleared and when complainant met the owner of the godown, Mr. Vishnubhai Gangbhai, complainant found that all accused NEUTRAL CITATION R/CR.MA/5689/2014 ORDER Vikramsinh Vadansinh Zala vs State Of Gujarat on 11 December, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/67354709/
3 DATED: 11/12/2024 undefined persons have taken the godown on rent from the owner of the godown, namely, Ashokbhai Gandalal Patel on rent at Rs.26,000/- per month and as per the statement of Ashokbhai Gandalal Patel, accused No.1 unloaded two trucks of cotton bales on 29.3.2014 and out of the unloaded material, certain materials were taken away by the accused.

sentences.text: Statement of Ashokbhai Gandalal Patel reveals that applicant No.1, happens to be friend of his brother, alongwith four other persons approached the owner of the godown to get the godown on rent.
Without making payment of goods, goods were sold away by the accused in the market.

Thus,
prima-facie involvement of petitioners is found in the commission of alleged offence.
Thus, at this stage it would not be appropriate to quash complaint by invoking the power under Section 482 of the Cr.P.C.. 6.1.

In the case of Vesa Holdings Private Limited (supra) the Apex Court has while discussing the issue on hand, observed that absence of ingredients of cheating at the time of making initial promise was absent.

There was a time bound Consultancy Contract between appellants and complainant to settle loan with NEUTRAL CITATION R/CR.MA/5689/2014 ORDER DATED:
11/12/2024 undefined Bank.
Non -payment of Consultancy fees does not attract the ingredients of cheating under Section 420 of the IPC. 6.2.
In the present case, it is not the allegation of complainant that there was a contract of sell and purchase of cotton between complainant and accused.
Accused purchased cotton from complainant on a promise to pay the price of goods.
And instead making payment sold away cotton in market.

6.3. In the case of Kunti and Another (supra),
an Agreement to Sell was executed between appellants and respondent No.2.
After a full fledged trial and after appreciation of evidence, judgment came to be passed against appellants.
The High Court confirmed the judgment of learned Chief Judicial Magistrate.
6.4. In the present case the trial has not yet commenced.
And this Court while exercising the powers under Section 482 of Cr.P.C. has only to consider that whether FIR, prima facie, disclose any commission of offence against petitioners.
Therefore, both the above decisions are not helpful to the petitioners.
NEUTRAL CITATION R/CR.MA/5689/2014 ORDER DATED: 11/12/2024 undefined 7.

At this stage, in a recent decision of the Hon'ble Supreme Court in case of Neeharika Infrastructure Pvt. Ltd. Vs. State of Maharashtra and Ors., reported in 2021 (19) SCC 401, is required to be referred to.

After taking into consideration the earlier decision of State of Haryana V.
Bhanaj Lal, reported in 1992 Supp (1) SCC 335 and others.

sentences.text:
The Hon'ble Supreme Court has observed in Paragraph Nos.10.3 & 33, which are as under:
"10.3.Then comes the celebrated decision of this Court in the case of Bhajan Lal (supra).

In the said decision, this Court considered in detail the scope of the High Court powers under section 482 Cr.P.C. and/or Article 226 of the Constitution of India to quash the FIR and referred to several judicial precedents and held that the High Court should not embark upon an inquiry into the merits and demerits of the allegations and quash the proceedings without allowing the investigating agency to complete its task.

At the same time, this Court identified the following cases in which FIR/complaint can be quashed:
"102.(1) Where the allegations made in the first information report or the complaint,
even if they are taken at their face value and accepted in their entirety do not prima Vikramsinh Vadansinh Zala vs State Of Gujarat on 11 December, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/67354709/
4 facie constitute any offence or make out a case against the accused.
NEUTRAL CITATION R/CR.MA/5689/2014 ORDER DATED: 11/12/2024 undefined (2) Where the allegations in the first information report and other materials, if any,
accompanying the FIR do not disclose a cognizable offence, justifying an investigation by police officers under section 156(1) of the Code except under an order of a Magistrate within the purview of section 155(2) of the Code.

entities.text: Vikramsinh Vadansinh Zala vs State Of Gujarat
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: (3) Where the uncontroverted allegations made in the FIR or complaint and the evidence collected in support of the same do not disclose the commission of any offence and make out a case against the accused.

(4) Where the allegations in the FIR do not constitute a cognizable offence but constitute only a non-cognizable offence, no investigation is permitted by a police officer without an order of a Magistrate as contemplated under section 155(2) of the Code.

(5) Where the allegations made in the FIR or complaint are so absurd and inherently improbable on the basis of which no prudent person can ever reach a just conclusion that there is sufficient ground for proceeding against the accused.

(6) Where there is an express legal bar engrafted in any of the provisions of the Code or the Act concerned (under which a criminal proceeding is instituted) to the institution and continuance of the proceedings and/or where there is a specific provision in the Code or the Act concerned, providing efficacious redress for the grievance of the aggrieved party.

NEUTRAL CITATION R/CR.MA/5689/2014 ORDER DATED: 11/12/2024 undefined (7) Where a criminal proceeding is manifestly attended with mala fide and/or where the proceeding is maliciously instituted with an ulterior motive for wreaking vengeance on the accused and with a view to spite him due to private and personal grudge."

In the above decision, the Apex Court came to the conclusion that;
"33.

sentences.text: Therefore, when the investigation by the police is in progress, the court should not go into the merits of the allegations in the FIR.
Police must be permitted to complete the investigation.
It would be premature to pronounce the conclusion based on hazy facts that the complaint/FIR does not deserve to be investigated or that it amounts to abuse of process of law.

After investigation, if the investigating officer finds that there is no substance in the application made by the complainant, the investigating officer may file an appropriate report/summary before the learned Magistrate which may be considered by the learned Magistrate in accordance with the known procedure;
xiii) The power under section 482 of Cr.P.C. is very wide, but conferment of wide power requires the court to be more cautious.
It casts an onerous and more diligent duty on the court;
NEUTRAL CITATION R/CR.MA/5689/2014 ORDER DATED: 11/12/2024 undefined xiv)

However, at the same time, the court, if it thinks fit, regard being had to the parameters of quashing and the self- restraint imposed by law, more particularly the parameters laid down by this Court in the cases of R.P. Kapur (supra) and Bhajan Lal (supra), has the jurisdiction to quash the FIR/complaint;
xv) When a prayer for quashing the FIR is made by the alleged accused and the court when it exercises the power under section 482 of Cr.P.C., only has to consider whether the allegations in the FIR disclose commission of a cognizable offence or not.

The court is not required to consider on merits whether or not the merits of the allegations make out a cognizable offence and the court has to permit the investigating agency/police to investigate the allegations in the FIR; xvi) The aforesaid parameters would be applicable and/or the aforesaid aspects are required to be considered by the High Court while passing an interim order in a quashing petition in exercise of powers under section 482 Cr.P.C. and/or under Article 226 of the Constitution of India.
However, an interim order of stay of investigation during the pendency of the quashing petition can be passed with circumspection.
Such an interim order should not require to be passed routinely, casually and/or mechanically.

Vikramsinh Vadansinh Zala vs State Of Gujarat on 11 December, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/67354709/
7

entities.text: Vikramsinh Vadansinh Zala vs State Of Gujarat on 11 December, 2024 Indian Kanoon
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Normally, when the investigation is in progress and the facts are hazy and the entire evidence/material is not before the High Court, the High Court should restrain NEUTRAL CITATION R/CR.MA/5689/2014 ORDER DATED: 11/12/2024 undefined itself from passing the interim order of not to arrest or "no coercive steps to be adopted" and the accused should be relegated to apply for anticipatory bail under section 438 Cr.P.C. before the competent court.

The High Court shall not and as such is not justified in passing the order of not to arrest and/or "no coercive steps" either during the investigation or till the investigation is completed and/or till the final report / charge-sheet is filed under section 173 Cr.P.C., while dismissing/disposing of the quashing petition under section 482 Cr.P.C. and/or under Article 226 of the Constitution of India.
xvii) Even in a case where the High Court is prima facie of the opinion that an exceptional case is made out for grant of interim stay of further investigation, after considering the broad parameters while exercising the powers under section 482 Cr.P.C. and/or under Article 226 of the Constitution of India referred to hereinabove, the High Court has to give brief reasons why such an interim order is warranted and/or is required to be passed so that it can demonstrate the application of mind by the Court and the higher forum can consider what was weighed with the High Court while passing such an interim order.
xviii) Whenever an interim order is passed by the High Court of "no coercive steps to be adopted"
within the aforesaid parameters, the High Court must clarify what does it mean by "no coercive steps to be adopted"

as the term "no coercive NEUTRAL CITATION R/CR.MA/5689/2014 ORDER DATED: 11/12/2024 undefined steps to be adopted" can be said to be too vague and/or broad which can be misunderstood and/or misapplied."

8. In view of the above decision given by the Apex Court in case of Neeharika Infrastructure Pvt. Ltd.
(Supra), it transpires that the power of quashing of criminal proceedings should be exercised very sparingly and with circumspection and that too in rarest of the rare cases and it was not justified for the Court in embarking upon an inquiry as to the reliability or genuineness or otherwise of the allegations made in the FIR or the complaint and that the inherent powers do not confer any arbitrary jurisdiction on the Court to act according to its whims and fancies.

It is well settled that at the stage when the High Court considers a petition for quashing criminal proceedings under Section 482 of the Cr.P.C, the allegations in the FIR must be read as they stand and it is only if on the face of the allegations that no cognizable offence, as alleged has been made out, that the Court may be justified in exercising its jurisdiction to quash.
NEUTRAL CITATION R/CR.MA/5689/2014 ORDER DATED: 11/12/2024 undefined 9.

Applying to the law laid down by the Hon'ble Supreme Court in case of Neeharika Infrastructure Pvt. Ltd. (supra) to the facts of the case in hand, this Court is of the firm opinion that this is not a fit case to entertain present application and to quash the criminal proceedings in exercising the powers under Section 482 of the Cr.P.C. at the threshold.
The submissions made on behalf of the applicants that he is an innocent and/or he has not committed any offence alleged is premature.

sentences.text: In view of the above and for the reasons stated herein above, no case is made out to quash the FIR / criminal proceedings at this stage while exercising the powers under Section 482 of the Cr.P.C.
Therefore, present petition fails and the same deserves to be dismissed and is accordingly dismissed.
Rule is discharged.
No order as to costs.
Interim relief, if any, stands vacated.
